dedupe_keys.name: open models and tools for seismic risk assessment applied to mainland portugal doctoral thesis

description: This case study is a doctoral thesis that develops open models and tools for seismic hazard and risk assessment and applies them to mainland Portugal. It was written by Vítor Silva at the Universidade de Aveiro and deposited in its repository on 7 March 2014, with abstracts in several languages. Seismic risk depends on hazard, exposure and vulnerability. The work built an open-source platform, available to anyone, that computes the distribution of losses or damage for a given scenario earthquake and the losses from all events that could occur in a region over a period; it also reviewed and applied analytical methods to derive the vulnerability of reinforced concrete buildings where observed damage data are lacking. Coverage: mainland Portugal's building stock. Access: the thesis is in the university's open repository. Licence: terms on the repository record, which was unreachable (HTTP 502) on 2026-09-26; free to read. Caveats: a 2014 study; the platform and models have since evolved elsewhere. Simulation uses: national scenario and probabilistic seismic loss estimation and retrofit prioritisation. Related records: the Irpinia empirical fragility data and the collapse volume ratio data.
name: Open models and tools for seismic risk assessment applied to mainland Portugal (doctoral thesis)
outcomes: The thesis developed an open-source platform that computes losses or damage for scenario earthquakes and probabilistic losses from all possible events, together with analytical vulnerability methods, and applied them to mainland Portugal.
resources_used: Open-source seismic hazard and risk platform developed in the thesis
Analytical vulnerability models for reinforced concrete buildings
